cues.text: The king's ghost looks at you for a while,
then hops onto the edge of his coffin with a mischievous grin,
and after making himself comfortable there,
he begins to tell you the history of his kingdom:
"A long, long time ago", he begins his story,
and his face is again that of an old, bitter man,
"this was a beautiful, peaceful and prosperous country,
in which all my subjects were justly and wisely ruled by me.
I resided in my castle on an island surrounded by crystal clear waters,
whose magnificent construction expressed the wealth and artistry of my people...
At that time I also employed a young magician named Zargon at my court,
who used to entertain me from time to time with his tricks.
He was talented, very talented in fact,
but I would never have suspected that he lived in
a secret chamber in the basement of my castle -
a room in which he carried out all his magical experiments:
he was obsessed with the crazy idea of artificially producing gold,
which he urgently needed in order to pay for the
lessons he took from the highest magicians in our country.
One day, however, his wishes came true:
he was accepted into the Seventh Circle of the Mages Guild,
which meant that his full magical power had developed and
he was entitled to use even the most powerful spells - yes,
he eventually became even more powerful than his former teachers,
who now followed the development of their most gifted student with great concern -
but in his infinite ambition he wanted even more: He wanted my throne!
But instead of fighting my noble knights in a brave and fair fight,
he turned to his magical powers and created an army of cruel, undead creatures...
One dark night - there was a thunderstorm as if the Day of Judgment had dawned -
he gathered these spawns of hell in front of my castle,
and when the clock on the tower struck midnight -
what a macabre irony of fate - the corpses of my ancestors,
who had been laid to rest in a crypt beneath the castle chambers,
rose from their coffins - and opened the gates!
It was little trouble for Zargon and his henchmen to take the castle within a few minutes:
no one had expected this attack - a fatal mistake...
After breaking down the door to my bedchamber,
Zargon's blackbloods led me away to their master,
who, without a word of explanation or apology,
drove the blade of his sword up to the hilt into my chest..."
